I estimated the ATT with inverse-propensity weighting. I fit a logistic propensity model on x0–x16 and gave each control the weight p/(1−p). The weighted control mean is then compared with the treated mean.

The outcome y is binary (employment status). The raw difference in means is 0.755 − 0.864 ≈ −0.108, which is misleading because the controls differ a lot from the treated group.

| Method | ATT estimate |
|---|---|
| IPW (the one I report) | 0.0103 |
| Regression adjustment, fit on controls | 0.0200 |
| OLS with a treatment dummy | 0.0168 |

I picked IPW as the headline number. The three estimates differ by about 0.01, so the result depends somewhat on the method chosen. All three put the effect near zero to slightly positive.

ANSWER: 0.010
